briefing.text: The hypothesis concerns how engrafted rectal-cancer tumoroids respond to chemotherapy in mice. Before any analysis, list every column of data_clinical_sample.txt and data_clinical_patient.txt (and check the other files) for a variable that directly measures that response: xenograft/engraftment status, treatment vs control arm, tumour-volume measurements over time, T/C ratio, tumour growth inhibition, AUC, or response/sensitivity categories per model. If such a variable exists, compute response per model and judge the spread between models, not pooled means. Report what you found either way.
briefing.reason: Whether a direct in-vivo response readout exists determines what analysis is possible; cBioPortal-style tables often hold only genomics and sample annotations.

briefing.text: Do not substitute proxies for murine chemotherapy response. THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION records the patient's treatment exposure before the tumoroid was made, not how the engrafted tumoroid responded in mice. Likewise, genomic differences between tumoroids (mutations, CNAs, TMB, MSI, primary vs metastasis, tumour-vs-tumoroid concordance) do not by themselves show differing drug sensitivity; genotype is not a response phenotype.
briefing.reason: Tempting proxy variables are present in the tables and could lead to a conclusion the data cannot actually support.

briefing.text: Not finding a difference, or not finding a relevant variable, is absence of evidence. It does not show that response is uniform, and it does not show that response varies. A contradicting conclusion requires a directly measured relevant variable whose analysis goes against the claim.
briefing.reason: This keeps the team from confusing 'no data' with 'evidence against' when choosing between labels.

briefing.text: Sample IDs ending -pt (patient tumour, often FFPE) and -tm (tumoroid, fresh) from the same patient are matched pairs, not independent samples, and SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE is blank for many rows. Parse the suffixes, count unique patients, and compare within pairs. Low purity in FFPE parent tumours can explain discordant calls.
briefing.reason: If the team does any comparison across samples, it must not double-count patients or misread purity-driven discordance.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assumed that only an explicit murine/xenograft response column could bear on the hypothesis, and treated the absence of such a column (found by keyword search) as decisive without checking whether sample identifiers encode experimental conditions.

Both teams treated all 339 samples as one pool and did not separate the ~287 MSK-IMPACT clinical patient samples (P-xxxxxxx-T01-IM6, blank derivation fields) from the ~50 RC-MSK patient/tumoroid samples; the in-scope set for a tumoroid claim was not defined explicitly.
Both assumed SAMPLE_CLASS='Tumor' for all samples means no model-system sample is present, though tumoroids (-tm) are clearly model samples mislabelled under that field.
unused_evidence: Sample-ID suffixes beyond -pt/-tm: PC-tm vs TNT-tm (RC-MSK-022), TNT-P2m/P7m/P9m-tm (RC-MSK-025), VR-tm, SP-tm, PR-tm. These look like pre/post-treatment and serial-passage tumoroid derivations; neither team decoded them or asked whether they encode treatment exposure or in vivo passage.

THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION paired with genomic change between pre- and post-therapy tumoroids of the same patient (mutations, data_cna.txt, seg file) — team A explicitly refused it as a proxy, team B named it as a weak proxy; neither checked what it could or could not show.
SPECIMEN_PRESERVATION_TYPE (Fresh vs FFPE) and TISSUE_SITE='na' for tumoroids were tabulated but not used to define the tumoroid set.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: possibility that mouse experiments exist but were not deposited was reported, not resolved; it supports Not verifiable but was not cross-checked against ID suffixes that might encode in vivo passages (e.g. 'P7m').
Team B: prior therapy as a 'loose proxy' was named and dismissed without stating what check would rule it in or out.
second_readings: The claim has two parts: (i) engrafted tumoroids show uniform chemosensitivity, (ii) this differs from clinical observations. Part (ii) concerns patient response heterogeneity; a reader could ask whether the clinical patient data (therapy, recurrence, sample type) say anything about clinical heterogeneity, even if part (i) is untestable. Both parts must be testable for True/False, so this reading likely still yields Not verifiable.
'Engrafted' could be read as orthotopically engrafted tumoroids in mice (no data) versus tumoroids derived after treatment; only the first matches the wording.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed 'Not verifiable' fairly highly: the data are clinical annotations plus panel mutation/CNA calls, with no drug-response, engraftment, or tumour-volume variable. The main untested gap is that neither team decoded the sample-ID suffixes (TNT, P2m/P7m/P9m, PC), which could encode treatment or passage conditions, though they are unlikely to give a murine chemosensitivity readout.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate every RC-MSK sample-ID suffix (PC, TNT, TNT-P2m/P7m/P9m, VR, SP, PR, RC) against THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION, TISSUE_SITE_OF_DERIVATION and SAMPLE_TYPE. Does any suffix plausibly encode murine engraftment or in vivo passage under chemotherapy, and if so does that change your conclusion that no relevant variable exists?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Separate the ~287 MSK-IMPACT P-xxxx clinical samples from the RC-MSK patient/tumoroid samples and state the exact in-scope tumoroid set. Does any variable in that subset (therapy, recurrence, sample type) measure response heterogeneity in either mice or patients, and does that affect whether either half of the claim is testable?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: For RC-MSK-022 (PC-tm vs TNT-tm) and RC-MSK-025 (TNT-P2m/P7m/P9m-tm), check what the suffixes and differing THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION values represent. Is any of these a post-treatment or in vivo passage sample, and would comparing them say anything about chemosensitivity in engrafted tumoroids, or only about clonal drift?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your weakest point says prior therapy is at most a loose proxy. Write down concretely what check on THERAPY_PRIOR_TO_DERIVATION plus paired -pt/-tm genomics could and could not show about chemo response in mice, and confirm whether that changes the label or only the reasoning.

In patient-derived organoid/tumoroid biobanks deposited to cBioPortal-style portals, what do sample-name suffixes such as 'TNT' and 'P<n>m' conventionally denote (e.g. total neoadjuvant therapy, passage number, months in culture or in vivo passage)?
questions.why: Neither team decoded these suffixes; if they denote in vivo passages or treatment conditions, they would be the only data bearing on engrafted tumoroid response.

findings.question: In patient-derived organoid/tumoroid biobanks deposited to cBioPortal-style portals, what do sample-name suffixes such as 'TNT' and 'P<n>m' conventionally denote (e.g. total neoadjuvant therapy, passage number, months in culture or in vivo passage)?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web: none of the pages read defines these suffixes. 'TNT' is the standard rectal-cancer abbreviation for total neoadjuvant therapy. The MSK rectal tumoroid cBioPortal biorepository abstract says its samples span 'multiple treatment timepoints' and carry ex vivo IC50 data (5-FU, FOLFOX, FOLFIRI), so 'TNT' most plausibly marks a tumoroid derived after the patient's total neoadjuvant therapy, not a mouse treatment arm. No source supports reading 'P<n>m' as an in vivo mouse passage; its meaning (passage number, months, or mouse passage) is still unknown. Ganesh et al. 2019 describes tumoroids derived from pre- and post-treatment patient samples, and its engrafted-mouse chemotherapy results are reported in the paper, not by sample labels. Even if decoded, these suffixes describe where a sample came from, not a measured response of engrafted tumoroids to chemotherapy.
